desc: Jim Corbett National Park is the oldest national park in India, established in 1936 as Hailey National Park. Located in the Nainital and Pauri Garhwal districts of Uttarakhand, it covers an area of 520.8 km². The park is famous for its Bengal tiger population and is a key part of Project Tiger, launched there in 1973. The diverse landscape includes hills, riverine belts, grasslands, and lakes. It is named after the renowned hunter-turned-conservationist Jim Corbett.
fact: It is the oldest national park in India, established in 1936 · It was the site of the launch of Project Tiger in 1973 · The park covers 520.8 km² in the foothills of the Himalayas · It is named after hunter-turned-conservationist Jim Corbett

desc: Kaziranga National Park is a UNESCO World Heritage Site located in the Golaghat and Nagaon districts of Assam. It is the world's largest habitat for the Indian one-horned rhinoceros, hosting about two-thirds of its global population. Established in 1905 as a reserve forest, it became a national park in 1974. The park also harbors significant populations of tigers, elephants, wild water buffalo, and swamp deer. The Brahmaputra River floods annually, enriching the park's ecosystem.
fact: It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and the world's largest habitat for the Indian one-horned rhinoceros · It hosts about two-thirds of the global one-horned rhino population · It was established in 1905 as a reserve forest · The annual Brahmaputra River floods enrich the park's ecosystem

desc: Kanha National Park is one of the largest and most famous national parks in India, located in the Maikal range of the Satpuras in Madhya Pradesh. Covering an area of 940 km², it was created in 1955. The park inspired Rudyard Kipling's 'The Jungle Book'. It is renowned for its successful conservation of the barasingha swamp deer, which was brought back from near-extinction. Kanha's landscape features sal and bamboo forests, grassy meadows, and ravines.
fact: It inspired Rudyard Kipling's 'The Jungle Book' · It is famous for the successful conservation of the barasingha swamp deer from near-extinction · It covers 940 km² in the Maikal range of the Satpuras · It is one of the largest national parks in India

desc: Bandhavgarh National Park is located in the Umaria district of Madhya Pradesh and is known for having one of the highest densities of Bengal tigers in India. The park derives its name from the ancient Bandhavgarh Fort, which sits on a hill within the park and has historical links to the Ramayana. The park covers an area of 448 km² and was declared a national park in 1968. Its terrain features rocky hills, grasslands, and dense forests with sal and bamboo trees.
fact: It has one of the highest densities of Bengal tigers in India · The ancient Bandhavgarh Fort sits within the park with links to the Ramayana · It was declared a national park in 1968 over 448 km² · The terrain features rocky hills, grasslands, and sal forests

desc: Ranthambore National Park is one of the largest national parks in northern India, located in the Sawai Madhopur district of Rajasthan. It is a premier tiger reserve and a major wildlife tourism destination. The park is famous for its frequent tiger sightings and the historic Ranthambore Fort, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, located within its boundaries. The park spans 392 km² with dry deciduous forests, open grasslands, and ancient stepwells and temples that dot the landscape.
fact: It is one of the largest national parks in northern India · The historic Ranthambore Fort, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, is within the park · It is famous for frequent tiger sightings · The park features dry deciduous forests and grasslands in scenic Rajasthan terrain

desc: Sundarbans National Park is a UNESCO World Heritage Site located in the Sundarbans delta of West Bengal, the world's largest mangrove forest. It is the largest tiger reserve in India and the only mangrove habitat of the Bengal tiger. The park covers an area of 1,330 km² and is part of a vast delta formed by the Ganges, Brahmaputra, and Meghna rivers. The Sundarbans are known for their unique ecosystem, tidal waterways, mudflats, and salt-tolerant mangrove trees.
fact: It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and the largest mangrove forest in the world · It is the only mangrove habitat of the Bengal tiger · It covers 1,330 km² in the Ganges-Brahmaputra-Meghna delta · The ecosystem features unique tidal waterways, mudflats, and salt-tolerant mangroves

desc: Gir National Park, also known as Sasan Gir, is a wildlife sanctuary and national park in the Junagadh district of Gujarat. It is the last and only natural habitat of the Asiatic lion, which was once widespread across Southwest Asia. Established in 1965, the park covers an area of 1,412 km². The successful conservation effort brought the Asiatic lion back from the brink of extinction, with the population growing from about 20 lions in 1913 to over 600 today. The park also supports leopards, hyenas, and over 300 bird species.
fact: It is the only natural habitat of the Asiatic lion in the world · The lion population grew from ~20 in 1913 to over 600 today · It was established in 1965 over 1,412 km² · It also supports leopards, hyenas, and over 300 bird species

desc: Periyar National Park, also known as Thekkady, is a protected area in the Idukki and Pathanamthitta districts of Kerala. Located in the Western Ghats, it was established as a tiger reserve in 1978. The park is centered around the Periyar Lake, an artificial reservoir created by the Mullaperiyar Dam. It is famous for its elephant populations, spice plantation tourism, and boat cruises on the lake. The park covers 305 km² and is notable for its tropical evergreen and moist deciduous forests.
fact: It is centered around the Periyar Lake, an artificial reservoir · It is famous for its elephant populations and spice plantation tourism · It was established as a tiger reserve in 1978 · Boat cruises on the lake offer unique wildlife viewing opportunities

desc: Manas National Park is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and a Project Tiger reserve located in the foothills of the Eastern Himalayas in Assam. It is also a Biosphere Reserve and an Elephant Reserve. The park covers 950 km² and is named after the Manas River, which flows through it. Manas is known for its rich biodiversity including the endangered pygmy hog, golden langur, and Assam roofed turtle. The park's landscape includes grasslands, tropical forests, and riverine habitats.
fact: It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site, Project Tiger reserve, and Biosphere Reserve · It is home to endangered species including the pygmy hog and golden langur · It is named after the Manas River that flows through it · It covers 950 km² in the foothills of the Eastern Himalayas

desc: Keoladeo National Park, formerly known as the Bharatpur Bird Sanctuary, is a UNESCO World Heritage Site located in Bharatpur, Rajasthan. It is one of the most important bird breeding and feeding grounds in the world, hosting over 370 bird species including the rare Siberian crane. The park spans 28.7 km² and was created as a wetland by the Maharaja of Bharatpur in the 18th century for duck hunting. It is a major wintering ground for migratory birds from Central Asia, Siberia, and China.
fact: It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and one of the most important bird breeding grounds in the world · It hosts over 370 bird species including the rare Siberian crane · It was created as a wetland in the 18th century for duck hunting · It is a major wintering ground for migratory birds from Central Asia and Siberia

desc: Hemis National Park is a high-altitude national park located in the Leh district of Ladakh. It is the largest national park in India, covering an area of 4,400 km². Established in 1981, the park is named after the famous Hemis Monastery. It is home to several rare and endangered species including the snow leopard, Tibetan wolf, Eurasian brown bear, and blue sheep. The park's stark landscape features high-altitude plateaus, deep gorges, and alpine meadows at elevations between 3,300 and 6,000 meters.
fact: It is the largest national park in India, covering 4,400 km² · It is home to the endangered snow leopard and Tibetan wolf · It is named after the famous Hemis Monastery · The park features high-altitude plateaus and alpine meadows up to 6,000 meters elevation

desc: Great Himalayan National Park is a UNESCO World Heritage Site located in the Kullu district of Himachal Pradesh. It covers an area of 1,171 km² in the western Himalayas at elevations ranging from 1,500 to 6,000 meters. Established in 1984, the park is known for its exceptional biodiversity including the western tragopan, Himalayan tahr, musk deer, and snow leopard. The park features pristine alpine meadows, glacial valleys, and dense deodar and pine forests. It is a popular destination for trekking and eco-tourism.
fact: It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site in the western Himalayas · It covers 1,171 km² with elevations from 1,500 to 6,000 meters · It is home to the western tragopan, Himalayan tahr, and snow leopard · It features alpine meadows, glacial valleys, and deodar forests

desc: Nanda Devi National Park is a UNESCO World Heritage Site located in the Chamoli district of Uttarakhand. It surrounds Nanda Devi, India's second-highest mountain at 7,816 meters. Established in 1982, the park covers 630 km² of pristine Himalayan wilderness. The park is famous for the Nanda Devi Sanctuary, a high-altitude basin encircled by a ring of peaks. It is home to rare species including the snow leopard, Himalayan musk deer, and bharal. The park is part of the Nanda Devi and Valley of Flowers UNESCO site.
fact: It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site surrounding Nanda Devi, India's second-highest peak · The Nanda Devi Sanctuary is a high-altitude basin encircled by peaks · It covers 630 km² of pristine Himalayan wilderness · It is home to snow leopards, musk deer, and bharal

desc: Valley of Flowers National Park is a UNESCO World Heritage Site located in the Chamoli district of Uttarakhand. It is renowned for its meadows of endemic alpine flowers and outstanding natural beauty. The park covers 87.5 km² at altitudes between 3,350 and 6,750 meters. Discovered by mountaineer Frank Smythe in 1931, the valley bursts into a vibrant carpet of flowers during the monsoon season. It is part of the Nanda Devi and Valley of Flowers UNESCO Biosphere Reserve.
fact: It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site famed for its alpine flower meadows · It was discovered by Frank Smythe in 1931 · The valley blooms with hundreds of flower species during the monsoon season · It is part of the Nanda Devi Biosphere Reserve

desc: Bandipur National Park is located in the Chamarajanagar district of Karnataka, in the Western Ghats. It was established as a tiger reserve in 1973 under Project Tiger and covers an area of 912 km². The park is part of the Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve, India's first biosphere reserve, and is contiguous with Nagarhole, Mudumalai, and Wayanad wildlife sanctuaries. Bandipur is known for its significant populations of tigers, Asian elephants, gaurs, and spotted deer. The park features dry deciduous forests, moist deciduous forests, and grassy swamps.
fact: It was established as a tiger reserve in 1973 under Project Tiger · It is part of the Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve, India's first biosphere reserve · It covers 912 km² in the Western Ghats · It has significant populations of tigers, Asian elephants, and gaurs
